proofs.proof_tex:
Fix rational \(\eta\) and rational \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\cup
\mathcal M_{\eta,1}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Choose
\(\psi^0\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), which exists by the definition of this
union.  Since \(\psi^0\in\Theta_\eta\), the mixture weights sum to one and
\(e_z\in[\eta,1-\eta]\).  Therefore
\[
p_1=\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_z e_z
   \geq \eta\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_z=\eta>0,
\qquad
p_0=\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_z(1-e_z)
   \geq \eta\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_z=\eta>0.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus every conditional probability defining \(H_d\) and \(N_d\) is defined.
Because the cells of \(P\) and \(\eta\) are rational, every coefficient in a
cleared branch system is rational.  Multiplying each atomic polynomial by a
positive common integer denominator produces an integer polynomial and
preserves its required equality or sign.

The algorithm in Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}one\text{-}collision\text{-}algorithm}\) enumerates
\[
2\cdot 2^3\cdot 2=32
\tag{2}
\]
labels \((k_0,s,\sigma)\): two proposed collided states, eight orientations,
and two relative alignments.  For each fixed label, the algorithm uses the
complete projection-and-lifting decision procedure whose correctness is
asserted by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}cad\text{-}quantifier\text{-}elimination}\).
That lemma gives a finite sign-invariant cylindrical decomposition for the
finite branch family and decides every Boolean combination of its atomic
signs.  Hence every branch computation terminates, and the finite loop in
(2) terminates.

There is a unique \(k_\ast\in\mathcal A\) for which
\(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_\ast}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Existence follows from the
assumed union.  If both values worked, then every member of the nonempty
global fiber would have its control terminal row collided at \(k=0\) and
noncollided at \(k=1\), while also having its control terminal row collided at
\(k=1\) and noncollided at \(k=0\).  This is impossible.  Thus uniqueness
holds.

For \(k_0=k_\ast\), Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}dimension\text{-}reduction}\) gives a surjective
reconstruction map
\[
\coprod_{s\in\{-1,1\}^3,\,\sigma\in\Sigma}
 \{y:\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\}
 \longrightarrow
 \widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P).
\tag{3}
\]
Because (3) is a map into the displayed fiber, every accepted point
reconstructs a feasible structural vector; because it is surjective, every
feasible structural vector occurs in at least one accepted chart.  Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}quotient\text{-}att}\) proves that simultaneous label
permutation leaves \(\tau\) unchanged.  Applying \(\tau\) to both sides of
(3) therefore yields exactly, rather than merely as an outer bound,
\[
\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)
=\bigcup_{s,\sigma}
 \left\{
 \tau\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right):
 \mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)
 \right\}.
\tag{4}
\]

For \(k_0\neq k_\ast\), suppose that a branch point \(y\) were accepted.
We verify reconstruction soundness directly, because the
dimension-reduction theorem itself is quantified over the correct stratum.
For every \((z,d,j)\), positivity of \(R_{zd}(i,j,k)\) makes
\(T_{zd}^R(i,j)>0\), and \(\rho_{zdj}(R)=0\) gives
\[
\frac{R_{zd}(0,j,1)}{T_{zd}^R(0,j)}
=\frac{R_{zd}(1,j,1)}{T_{zd}^R(1,j)}
=\kappa_{zd3j}^R.
\tag{5}
\]
After expanding the two denominators, equality of the first two fractions is
exactly the rank-one equality.  Consequently
\[
R_{zd}(i,j,k)=T_{zd}^R(i,j)B(\kappa_{zd3j}^R;k).
\tag{6}
\]
The definitions of \(S^R,w^R,u^R,a^R\), again with positive denominators,
give
\[
T_{zd}^R(i,j)
=w_{zd}^R B(u_{zd}^R;i)B(a_{zdi}^R;j).
\tag{7}
\]
For each aligned pair, \(\gamma_{zi}^{\sigma}(R)=0\) and positivity of both
initial-state masses imply
\[
a_{z1i}^R=a_{\sigma(z),0,i}^R.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus (6)--(8) supply the common pre-treatment transition required by the
structural model.  The recovered weights obey \(\sum_z w_{zd}^R=1\).  With
\[
\pi_z=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0}^R+p_1w_{z1}^R,
\qquad
e_z=\frac{p_1w_{z1}^R}{\pi_z},
\tag{9}
\]
one has \(\sum_z\pi_z=p_0+p_1=1\) and
\[
\pi_ze_z=p_1w_{z1}^R,
\qquad
\pi_z(1-e_z)=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0}^R.
\tag{10}
\]
The box atoms put every recovered primitive in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).
Equations (6)--(10), the terminal split identities
\(H_d=R_{1d}+R_{2d}\) and
\(N_d=v_{1dk}R_{1d}+v_{2dk}R_{2d}\), and (10) show cell by cell that the
reconstructed structural vector generates \(P\).  The collision and strict
orientation atoms put it in \(\Theta_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y)
 \in\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)
 \subseteq\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P).
\tag{11}
\]
But membership of \(P\) in
\(\mathcal M_{\eta,k_\ast}^{1\mathrm c}\) requires every element of the last
fiber in (11) to lie in \(\Theta_{\eta,k_\ast}^{1\mathrm c}\), whereas the
reconstruction in (11) lies in \(\Theta_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\).  These two
strata are disjoint because one requires collision at \(k_0\) and
noncollision at \(1-k_0\), while the other requires the reverse.  This
contradiction proves that all wrong-state branches are rejected and that
\(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)=\varnothing\) there.  Consequently (4),
with the empty case included, proves exactness for each \(k_0\).

For the joint output, adjoin retained coordinates \((q_3,q_4)\) and the two
equalities
\[
q_t=\tau_t\!\left(
 \operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right),
\qquad t\in\{3,4\}.
\tag{12}
\]
All denominators cleared in (12) are positive on the branch by construction,
so clearing preserves equality.  Applying the cited quantifier-elimination
lemma to eliminate \(y\) gives a quantifier-free Boolean combination of
integer-polynomial sign conditions in \((q_3,q_4)\).  Disjoining these
formulas over the labels in (2) and using (4) proves that the returned joint
formula defines exactly the attained joint image.

It remains to prove the marginal and witness assertions.  The parameter
space \(\Theta_\eta\) is compact by definition, and \(F\) is polynomial,
hence continuous.  Therefore
\[
K(P)=\{\psi\in\Theta_\eta:F(\psi)=P\}
\tag{13}
\]
is compact.  Exclusivity at \(k_\ast\) gives
\(K(P)=\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_\ast}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  Equation (1) bounds
the only denominator in \(w_{z1}\) away from zero, and the recursions defining
\(m_{z3}\) and \(m_{z4}\) are polynomial in the primitive probabilities.
Thus \(\psi\mapsto\tau(\psi;P)\) is continuous on \(K(P)\).  Its joint image
and its two coordinate images are compact; in particular, every coordinate
endpoint and every isolated coordinate value is attained by a feasible
\(\psi\).

Each marginal is semialgebraic by (12) and quantifier elimination.  The
finitely many nonzero univariate polynomials in its quantifier-free formula
have finitely many roots.  Those roots partition the real line into finitely
many points and open intervals on each of which every atomic sign is
constant.  Hence the marginal is a finite union of points and intervals.
Its compactness makes it closed and bounded, so after merging adjacent
pieces it is a finite ordered union of closed intervals and isolated points.
For rational input, the cited CAD lemma supplies every boundary root as a
real-algebraic number with a square-free integer polynomial, a rational
isolating interval, and its Thom derivative-sign encoding.

Finally, fix a marginal endpoint or isolated value.  Attainment above gives
a nonempty section of (13), and (3) places an attaining representation in an
accepted labeled chart.  Lifting the endpoint section in (12) supplies a
real-algebraic sample point \(y\); the rational reconstruction formulas then
supply the promised real-algebraic feasible \(\psi\).  If a branch is
discarded, sign-invariant lifting covers its candidate cells and the decision
of its original Boolean formula is false on every one of them.  Recording for
each such cell a first original atom with the wrong sign is therefore an exact
finite infeasibility certificate.  This is precisely Collins real quantifier
elimination after the ten-coordinate reduction; no step changes the generic
projection schedule, so no generic worst-case complexity improvement is
claimed.

proposed.statement:
For rational \(\eta\) and rational
\(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\cup
\mathcal M_{\eta,1}^{1\mathrm c}\),
\(\mathsf{OneCollisionATT}(P,\eta)\) terminates after examining exactly
thirty-two labeled \((k_0,s,\sigma)\) branches and returns, for each \(k_0\),
exactly the attained joint image \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) as a
quantifier-free semialgebraic formula. It returns each nonempty
\(\mathcal I_{k_0,t}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) as a finite ordered union of closed
intervals and isolated points with Thom-encoded real-algebraic endpoints, a
reconstructed feasible latent representation for every endpoint and isolated
component, and an exact infeasibility certificate for every discarded branch.
The theorem claims equivalence to Collins real quantifier elimination after
the proved ten-coordinate reduction and claims no improvement in generic
worst-case CAD complexity.
proposed.justification: Complete quantifier elimination after the established ten-coordinate reduction returns the attained causal region without convexifying disconnected components.
proposed.gap: General CAD does not itself provide the model-specific causal reconstruction, fixed branch inventory, or latent endpoint-witness grammar.
proposed.consumer: The public ak backend can report exact marginal components, algebraic endpoints, and a feasible representation attaining each reported boundary.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses reconstruction soundness from the explicit ten-variable system even when auditing the wrong proposed collided state, so this direct dependency is made explicit; the formal claim is unchanged.

proposed.name: Exact one-collision persistence family
proposed.construction:
For every \(\vartheta\in(-1/100,1/100)\), let
\(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) be obtained from \(\psi^{\diamond}\) by
replacing only \(c_{130}=3/10\) by
\(c_{130}(\vartheta)=3/10+\vartheta\), and let
\(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\) be obtained from
\(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\) by the identical replacement of its treated
coordinate. All other primitive coordinates are unchanged. Define
\(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}=F(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})\). Thus
\(\psi^{\diamond}_{0}=\psi^{\diamond}\),
\(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{0}=\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\), and
\(P^{\diamond}_{0}=P^{\diamond}\). The specialization \(\eta=1/10\),
\(\vartheta=0\), and \(P=P^\diamond\) is the fixed input governed by
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}p\text{-}diamond\text{-}execution\text{-}certificate\text{-}contract}\).
The external identifier
\(\texttt{art:p-diamond-onecollisionatt-v1}\) is reserved for a literal
payload and deterministic replay satisfying that contract. A record that
supplies candidate leaves, branch dispositions, output formulas, or endpoints
before deriving them from projection and lifting does not bear this
identifier.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This complete replacement preserves the persistence family, fixes its zero-perturbation specialization as the bounded execution input, and prevents the rejected predeclared-leaf fixture from being called the canonical artifact.

proposed.name: Exact one-collision ATT algorithm
proposed.construction:
\(\mathsf{OneCollisionATT}(P,\eta)\) takes reduced rational encodings of
\(\eta\) and the thirty-two cells of \(P\); enumerates exactly
\(2\cdot2^3\cdot2=32\) labeled branches \((k_0,s,\sigma)\); builds each
ten-variable system \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}\); performs the fixed Collins
projection and signed Sturm--Habicht lifting in
\(\mathrm{def{:}observable\text{-}sign\text{-}certificate}\); and projects
each retained cell through
\(\tau(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P)\). The joint image is
returned as a quantifier-free Boolean combination of integer-polynomial sign
conditions in \((\tau_3,\tau_4)\). Each marginal is returned as an ordered
finite union of closed intervals and isolated points whose endpoints have a
square-free integer polynomial, rational isolating interval, and Thom sign
sequence. Every endpoint carries a reconstructed real-algebraic \(\psi\) and
its \((k_0,s,\sigma)\) label. An exact certificate for a discarded branch
serializes the complete original cleared polynomial family, the recursive
all-pairs projection data and their exact identities, the signed
Sturm--Habicht lifting and root-isolation data, and a covering of every lifted
candidate cell by a first violated original atom. Branch dispositions,
quantifier-free outputs, endpoints, and witnesses must be derived from those
records and cannot be accepted as predeclared inputs.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The prior certificate grammar was too weak to distinguish a replay-derived CAD execution from a fixture with predeclared leaves and outputs; the replacement makes projection identities, lifting coverage, and derivation of dispositions mandatory.

proposed.name: Fixed P-diamond execution-certificate contract
proposed.construction:
At \(\eta=1/10\), \(\vartheta=0\), and \(P=P^\diamond\), a machine-readable
record bearing the external identifier
\(\texttt{art:p-diamond-onecollisionatt-v1}\) is a canonical execution
certificate for \(\mathsf{OneCollisionATT}\) if and only if all of the
following data and checks are present.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The input section contains all thirty-two reduced rational cells
\(P^\diamond_{ijkld}\) literally and verifies by exact arithmetic that their
sum is one, that \(p_0=p_1=1/2\), and that both \(\psi^\diamond\) and
\(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\) generate every displayed cell. From these
inputs alone it derives every entry of \(H\) and \(N\), every collision minor
\(\chi\), and the complete instantiated original family
\(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}\), recording canonical polynomial identifiers and
exact rational values or signs whenever a polynomial is specialized to a
sample.
\item For every one of the thirty-two labels \((k_0,s,\sigma)\), the record
contains every original cleared integer equality, weak inequality, and strict
inequality with a canonical polynomial identifier. At each of the ten
projection coordinates it contains contents, all coefficients and leading
coefficients, discriminants, and the resultants and signed principal
subresultant coefficients for every unordered pair in the complete current
family, together with exact determinant, pseudo-remainder, or Bezout
identities that verify those projected polynomials.
\item The lifting record contains the signed Sturm--Habicht sequences, exact
root-isolating intervals and Thom signs, section and sector sample encodings,
parent--child incidence data, and an algebraically checkable proof that the
children cover every real stack over every retained parent cell.
\item Each rejected branch is derived by evaluating a first violated original
atom on every lifted candidate cell. Each accepted branch, reconstructed
structural vector, cellwise equality \(F(\psi)=P^\diamond\), ATT value,
quantifier-free output, endpoint isolator, and Thom sign is derived from the
accepted lifted cells, rather than supplied as an input constant.
\item A deterministic exact checker begins only with the literal input cells
and the declared polynomial order, verifies every projection and lifting
identity and every coverage relation, derives all branch dispositions and
outputs, verifies the canonical serialization, and rejects a payload with a
predeclared leaf list or output formula that lacks such derivations.
\end{enumerate}
This contract defines validity, not existence: a reduced-rational regression
fixture containing the correct PMF and proposed witness values is not by
itself a canonical execution certificate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This bounded contract gives the machine identifier an exact, replay-verifiable meaning while making no false existence claim for the currently incomplete fixture.

prose_updates.tldr: On the compact binary four-period model, the completed singular result is the exclusive stratum with distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one collided control terminal row. Terminal splitting reduces its forty-coordinate labeled fiber to sixteen ten-variable orientation/alignment charts for each collided state. A corrected full Collins certificate decides branch feasibility and aggregate-ATT constancy in principle, and the exact theorem returns the attained, possibly disconnected sharp image with endpoint witnesses. The fixed P-diamond regression fixture exactly reproduces its PMF, rational witnesses, ATT values, and endpoint encodings, but it is not presented as a canonical algorithm execution because a replay-generated all-pairs projection tree, signed lifting record, and exhaustive algebraic coverage certificate have not yet been supplied.

project_justification.fill: The project proves the arm-label-aware ten-coordinate reconstruction, uses complete Collins quantifier elimination to characterize the exact attained one-collision ATT image, and supplies auxiliary finite-sample full-PMF coverage. A separate injective one-parameter family proves persistent two-value ambiguity. For the fixed P-diamond specialization, exact-rational preprocessing and witness checks are available as a regression fixture; they are not counted as a canonical OneCollisionATT execution until the complete projection-and-lifting certificate is generated and replay-verified.

prose_updates.interpretation: A reported ATT sign on this merger stratum is identified only when the complete two-copy certificate rejects every feasible unequal-ATT pair across all orientations and both relative alignments. Otherwise the estimand is the attained set itself, which may be disconnected and must not be replaced by its convex hull. The fixed P-diamond files currently audit rational inputs and proposed witnesses; they do not certify exhaustive CAD execution and should not be described as a canonical backend trace.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The completed algebra covers only laws whose entire compact fiber has distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one specified collided control terminal row. The complete certificate remains full Collins quantifier elimination and may have its generic worst-case cost. The available P-diamond regression fixture predeclares its four leaves and output formulas and therefore does not yet instantiate the required projection identities, signed Sturm--Habicht lifting, or algebraic cell-coverage proof. No endpoint, Hausdorff, or branch-persistence consistency theorem is claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Completed claims are quotient invariance, the forty-to-ten one-collision reduction, the complete thirty-two-branch feasibility and ATT-constancy characterization, the exact attained stratum-restricted region, the explicit positive-dimensional two-value family, and uniformly honest finite-sample full-PMF inversion. Exact P-diamond PMF, reconstruction, and ATT regression checks are available, but no canonical machine execution artifact is claimed without a replay-derived complete Collins projection and lifting certificate. No result is claimed for other terminal-collision strata, an unboxed singular class, a global collision atlas, near-collision theory, Hausdorff or ordered-endpoint consistency, or a compressed irredundant sign basis.

statement_notes.justification: Complete quantifier elimination after the established ten-coordinate reduction returns the attained causal region without convexifying disconnected components; this formal theorem does not by itself certify any particular serialized execution trace.
statement_notes.gap: General CAD supplies existence and correctness of the exact procedure but not a replay-generated P-diamond projection tree, lifting coverage certificate, or canonical byte serialization.
statement_notes.consumer: The public ak backend may use the theorem's output grammar, while the current P-diamond files should be treated only as an exact-rational regression fixture until the full execution certificate is generated.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,3/20)\) and \(\vartheta\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta|<1/100\).  We use four elementary techniques: direct full-path factorization to compare the two proposed representations, a two-component spectral factorization to recover the treated arm, affine-mixture elimination to recover the control arm, and finite enumeration of the two possible cross-arm alignments.

First consider support and the probability box.  The only primitive that varies with \(\vartheta\) satisfies
\[
 \frac{29}{100}<c_{130}(\vartheta)=\frac{3}{10}+\vartheta<\frac{31}{100}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Every other primitive coordinate in either displayed representation belongs to \([1/5,4/5]\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}eta\text{-}domain}\) gives \(\eta<3/20<1/5\) and \(U=1-\eta>17/20>4/5\).  Thus (1) and the definition of \(\Theta_\eta\) imply
\[
 \psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta},\ \psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\in\Theta_\eta,
 \tag{2}
\]
indeed with strict slack at every face of the box.  In particular, every event on which we condition below has strictly positive probability.

For \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\), direct use of the Bernoulli factorization defining \(F\) gives
\[
 p_1=\frac12\frac35+\frac12\frac25=\frac12,
 \qquad p_0=\frac12,
 \qquad (w_{10},w_{20})=\left(\frac25,\frac35\right),
 \qquad (w_{11},w_{21})=\left(\frac35,\frac25\right).
 \tag{3}
\]
For \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\), the latent masses are \((3/5,2/5)\) and both assignment probabilities are \(1/2\), so its posterior weights are \((3/5,2/5)\) in each arm.  Its treated components and their weights therefore equal those in the first representation.  In the control arm it assigns weight \(3/5\) to the former second component and weight \(2/5\) to the former first component.  Hence, for each \(i,j,k,l,d\in\mathcal A\), commutativity of the two summands in the defining formula for \(F\) yields
\[
 F(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})_{ijkld}
 =F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta})_{ijkld}
 =P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta,ijkld}.
 \tag{4}
\]

We next prove that (4) exhausts the full global fiber.  For an arm \(d\), define the observable \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrix, with row index \(l\) and column index \(i\),
\[
 Q_{jk}^{d}(l,i)
 =P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=k,X_4=l\mid D=d).
 \tag{5}
\]
The division in (5) is valid because (3) gives \(p_d=1/2\).  In any two-type representation of this conditional law, put
\[
 q_{zj}=\kappa_{zd3j},\qquad v_{zk}=\kappa_{zd4k},\qquad
 V_k=\begin{pmatrix}1-v_{1k}&1-v_{2k}\\ v_{1k}&v_{2k}\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad S_j(z,i)=w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zi};j).
 \tag{6}
\]
Expanding the definition of \(F\) cell by cell gives the exact factorization
\[
 Q_{jk}^{d}
 =V_k\operatorname{diag}\!\bigl(B(q_{1j};k),B(q_{2j};k)\bigr)S_j.
 \tag{7}
\]

Consider \(d=1\).  In the displayed representation,
\[
 |\det V_0|=\frac35,
 \qquad |\det V_1|=\frac25.
 \tag{8}
\]
Since \(a_{10}=a_{20}=3/10\) and \(a_{11}=a_{21}=4/5\), the determinant in (6) is
\[
 \det S_j=w_{11}w_{21}B(3/10;j)B(4/5;j)(u_{21}-u_{11}),
\]
and therefore
\[
 \det S_0=\frac{21}{3125},
 \qquad \det S_1=\frac{36}{3125}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Every factor \(B(q_{zj};k)\) in the treated version of (7) is at least \(1/5\) for \(|\vartheta|<1/100\).  Taking determinants in (7) and applying (8)--(9) proves the uniform observable rank bound
\[
 |\det Q_{jk}^{1}|
 \ge \frac25\left(\frac15\right)^2\frac{21}{3125}
 =\frac{42}{390625}>0
 \qquad(j,k\in\mathcal A).
 \tag{10}
\]

For completeness, we now perform the spectral recovery rather than merely invoking mixture identifiability.  Cancellation in (7), justified by (10), gives
\[
 Q_{01}^{1}(Q_{00}^{1})^{-1}Q_{10}^{1}(Q_{11}^{1})^{-1}
 =V_1\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\lambda_1(\vartheta),\lambda_2\bigr)V_1^{-1},
 \tag{11}
\]
where
\[
 \lambda_1(\vartheta)
 =\frac{\operatorname{odds}(3/10+\vartheta)}{\operatorname{odds}(7/10)}
 =\frac{3(3+10\vartheta)}{7(7-10\vartheta)},
 \qquad
 \lambda_2
 =\frac{\operatorname{odds}(3/5)}{\operatorname{odds}(1/5)}=6.
 \tag{12}
\]
Here \(\operatorname{odds}(r)=r/(1-r)\), and all denominators are positive by (1).  Monotonicity of the first rational function on the interval in (1) gives
\[
 0<\lambda_1(\vartheta)<\frac{31}{161},
 \qquad
 \bigl(\lambda_2-\lambda_1(\vartheta)\bigr)^2
 >\left(\frac{935}{161}\right)^2>0.
 \tag{13}
\]
Thus the two one-dimensional eigenspaces of the observable matrix on the left side of (11) are distinct and are exactly the two column spans of \(V_1\).  Each such span has a unique probability-vector representative, obtained by normalizing its positive entries to sum to one.  This recovers \(V_1\) up to permutation.  In the same ordering,
\[
 Q_{00}^{1}(Q_{01}^{1})^{-1}V_1
 =V_0\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{1-q_{10}}{q_{10}},
                                  \frac{1-q_{20}}{q_{20}}\right),
 \tag{14}
\]
so positive column normalization recovers \(V_0\).  Finally, (7) implies
\[
 S_j=(V_0)^{-1}Q_{j0}^{1}+(V_1)^{-1}Q_{j1}^{1}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Indeed, the two summands in (15) are respectively
\(\operatorname{diag}(1-q_{1j},1-q_{2j})S_j\) and
\(\operatorname{diag}(q_{1j},q_{2j})S_j\).  Their positive row sums determine \(q_{zj}\); the row sums of \(S_0+S_1\) determine \(w_{z1}\); and positive entry ratios determine \(u_{z1}\) and \(a_{zi}\).  Since the matrices \(Q_{jk}^{1}\) are fixed by the observed law, (10)--(15) apply to every alternative representation in the fiber.  Consequently the entire treated decomposition is unique up to a common type permutation.  In particular, every compatible representation satisfies
\[
 a_{10}=a_{20}=\frac3{10},
 \qquad a_{11}=a_{21}=\frac45.
 \tag{16}
\]

It remains to recover the control arm, for which the conditional law does not depend on \(\vartheta\).  Define the observable conditional moments
\[
 g_{ij}=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_3=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0),
 \qquad
 h_{ij}=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_3=1,X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0).
 \tag{17}
\]
Their conditioning events have positive mass by (2).  Exact substitution into (4) gives
\[
 (g_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}41/115&111/230\\[2pt]23/45&11/30\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 (h_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}103/575&174/575\\[2pt]49/225&14/75\end{pmatrix},
 \tag{18}
\]
and
\[
 P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=0,D=0)=\frac12
 \quad(i,j\in\mathcal A).
 \tag{19}
\]

In any compatible control decomposition, label its types temporarily and put
\[
 \lambda_i=P(Z=1\mid X_1=i,D=0),
 \qquad q_{zj}=\kappa_{z0,3,j},
 \qquad v_{zk}=\kappa_{z0,4,k}.
\]
Equation (16) makes the conditional law of \(X_2\) given \((X_1,D=0,Z=z)\) independent of \(z\).  Bayes' formula, with positive denominators ensured by (2), therefore shows that the posterior type probability after additionally conditioning on \(X_2=j\) is still \(\lambda_i\).  Hence
\[
 g_{ij}=\lambda_iq_{1j}+(1-\lambda_i)q_{2j}.
 \tag{20}
\]
The observable differences computed from (18) are
\[
 g_{00}-g_{10}=-\frac{32}{207},
 \qquad
 g_{01}-g_{11}=\frac8{69}.
 \tag{21}
\]
Since \(g_{0j}-g_{1j}=(\lambda_0-\lambda_1)(q_{1j}-q_{2j})\), (21) proves
\[
 \lambda_0\ne\lambda_1,
 \qquad q_{1j}\ne q_{2j}\quad(j\in\mathcal A).
 \tag{22}
\]

Multiplying (19) by the positive conditional mass of \(X_3=0\), and using (20), gives for each \(i,j\)
\[
 \lambda_i(1-q_{1j})(v_{10}-1/2)
 +(1-\lambda_i)(1-q_{2j})(v_{20}-1/2)=0.
 \tag{23}
\]
For fixed \(j\), the determinant of the two equations indexed by \(i=0,1\) equals
\[
 (\lambda_0-\lambda_1)(1-q_{1j})(1-q_{2j}).
 \tag{24}
\]
It is nonzero by (22) and the strict upper box bound \(q_{zj}\le U<1\).  The unique solution of (23) is therefore
\[
 v_{10}=v_{20}=\frac12.
 \tag{25}
\]
This derives, rather than assumes, the single collided control terminal row.

For the noncollided row, (18) and (21) yield
\[
 \beta_j=\frac{h_{0j}-h_{1j}}{g_{0j}-g_{1j}},
 \qquad (\beta_0,\beta_1)=\left(\frac14,1\right),
 \tag{26}
\]
and
\[
 h_{ij}-\beta_jg_{ij}=c_j,
 \qquad (c_0,c_1)=\left(\frac9{100},-\frac9{50}\right).
 \tag{27}
\]
Both sides of (27) are affine functions of \(\lambda_i\).  Since \(\lambda_0\ne\lambda_1\), equality at these two distinct arguments forces equality of the two component intercepts and slopes.  Thus
\[
 q_{z0}(v_{z1}-1/4)=\frac9{100},
 \qquad
 q_{z1}(v_{z1}-1)=-\frac9{50}
 \quad(z=1,2).
 \tag{28}
\]
Likewise, the two identities obtained from (18),
\[
 g_{i1}=\frac34(1-g_{i0})\quad(i=0,1),
\]
hold at the two distinct mixing probabilities \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1\).  Applying the same affine-mixture argument to (20) gives
\[
 q_{z1}=\frac34(1-q_{z0})\quad(z=1,2).
 \tag{29}
\]
Writing \(x=q_{z0}\) and \(v=v_{z1}\), equations (28)--(29) reduce to
\[
 x(v-1/4)=\frac9{100},
 \qquad
 (1-x)(1-v)=\frac6{25}.
\]
Eliminating \(x\) yields the factored equation
\[
 50v^2-55v+14=(5v-2)(10v-7)=0.
 \tag{30}
\]
The two roots are distinct.  Equation (22) rules out assigning the same root to both types.  Substitution back into (28)--(29) therefore recovers the unordered control triples exactly as
\[
 (q_{z0},q_{z1},v_{z1})
 \in\left\{
 \left(\frac35,\frac3{10},\frac25\right),
 \left(\frac15,\frac35,\frac7{10}\right)
 \right\}.
 \tag{31}
\]

Label the second triple in (31) as type one.  Equations (18) and (20) then give
\[
 (\lambda_0,\lambda_1)=\left(\frac{14}{23},\frac29\right).
 \tag{32}
\]
The observed control probability \(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_1=0\mid D=0)=23/50\), together with Bayes' formula and (32), gives
\[
 w_{10}=\frac{23}{50}\frac{14}{23}+\frac{27}{50}\frac29=\frac25,
 \qquad
 u_{10}=\frac{(27/50)(2/9)}{2/5}=\frac3{10}.
 \tag{33}
\]
The other control component consequently has weight \(3/5\) and initial-state probability \(7/10\).  Thus the control decomposition is unique up to permutation.  As an explicit rank check, the determinants in (24), for \(j=0,1\), are respectively
\[
 \frac{128}{1035}\quad\hbox{and}\quad\frac{112}{1035},
 \tag{34}
\]
so no division or inversion in the control recovery approaches a zero denominator along the \(\vartheta\)-family.

The treated and control decompositions are now separately unique up to permutation.  Their only remaining ambiguity is their relative alignment.  The definitions of \(w_{zd}\), \(p_d\), and \(e_z\) imply
\[
 \pi_z=p_0w_{z0}+p_1w_{z1},
 \qquad
 e_z=\frac{p_1w_{z1}}{\pi_z}.
 \tag{35}
\]
Pairing the control weights \((2/5,3/5)\) with treated weights \((3/5,2/5)\) in the displayed order gives \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(1/2,1/2)\) and \((e_1,e_2)=(3/5,2/5)\).  Crossing the pairing gives \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(3/5,2/5)\) and \((e_1,e_2)=(1/2,1/2)\).  Both satisfy the strict box bounds in (2), and the two possible bijections between two recovered component sets leave no third alignment.  Therefore
\[
 \widetilde\Phi_\eta(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\{\sigma\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}:\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\}
 \cup
 \{\sigma\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}:\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\}.
 \tag{36}
\]

For either relative alignment and either simultaneous labeling, the first terminal difference in the definition of \(\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\) vanishes, while the absolute values of the other three terminal differences are
\[
 \left(\left|\frac7{10}-\frac25\right|,
       \left|\frac15-\frac45\right|,
       \left|\frac7{10}-\frac3{10}\right|\right)
 =\left(\frac3{10},\frac35,\frac25\right).
 \tag{37}
\]
Thus every member of the nonempty global fiber (36) belongs to \(\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\), equations (2), (4), (36), and (37) prove
\[
 P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c},
 \]
and they also prove that the global and one-collision quotient fibers coincide and contain exactly the two classes represented by \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) and \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\).

It remains to evaluate the causal target on these two attainable representations.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}quotient\text{-}att}\) proves that \(\tau\) is invariant under simultaneous type permutation, so one representative of each quotient class suffices.  For the displayed alignment, the recursive definitions of \(m_{z2},m_{z3},m_{z4}\) give
\[
 (m_{12},m_{13},m_{14})=\left(\frac12,\frac25,\frac{29}{50}\right),
 \qquad
 (m_{22},m_{23},m_{24})=\left(\frac35,\frac{21}{50},\frac{229}{500}\right).
 \tag{38}
\]
Only the type-one treated transition from \(X_2=0\) changes with \(\vartheta\).  By (3) and \(P(X_2=0\mid Z=1,D=1)=1-m_{12}=1/2\), direct expectation under \(F\) yields
\[
 O_3(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\frac{111}{250}+w_{11}(1-m_{12})\vartheta
 =\frac{111}{250}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10}.
 \tag{39}
\]
For that type, \(c_{141}-c_{140}=7/10-1/5=1/2\), so iterated expectation gives
\[
 O_4(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\frac{259}{500}+w_{11}(1-m_{12})(c_{141}-c_{140})\vartheta
 =\frac{259}{500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}.
 \tag{40}
\]
For the crossed alignment, the same untreated recursions instead give
\[
 (m_{12},m_{13},m_{14})=\left(\frac12,\frac9{20},\frac{91}{200}\right),
 \qquad
 (m_{22},m_{23},m_{24})=\left(\frac35,\frac{11}{25},\frac{147}{250}\right).
 \tag{41}
\]
Using the treated posterior weights \((3/5,2/5)\), equations (38) and (41) imply, respectively,
\[
 \left(\sum_z w_{z1}m_{z3},\sum_z w_{z1}m_{z4}\right)
 =\left(\frac{51}{125},\frac{332}{625}\right)
 \tag{42}
\]
and
\[
 \left(\sum_z w_{z1}m_{z3},\sum_z w_{z1}m_{z4}\right)
 =\left(\frac{223}{500},\frac{2541}{5000}\right).
 \tag{43}
\]
Subtracting (42)--(43) from the observed treated means (39)--(40), exactly as required by the definition of \(\tau\), gives
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta};P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\left(\frac9{250}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},
         -\frac{33}{2500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right)
 \tag{44}
\]
and
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta};P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\left(-\frac1{500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},
         \frac{49}{5000}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right).
 \tag{45}
\]
Fiber exhaustion in (36) proves attainability and excludes every other value, so (44)--(45) are the sharp joint identified image rather than merely an outer bound.  Their date-three difference is \(19/500\), and their date-four difference in absolute value is \(23/1000\), independently of \(\vartheta\).  Projection gives the asserted marginal two-point images.  Setting \(\vartheta=0\) yields
\[
 \mathcal I_{0,3}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-1/500,9/250\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_{0,4}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-33/2500,49/5000\}.
 \tag{46}
\]

Finally, direct expansion of the full-path cell \((i,j,k,l,d)=(0,0,1,1,1)\) gives
\[
 P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta,00111}-P^{\diamond}_{0,00111}
 =\left(\frac12\frac35\frac35\frac7{10}\frac7{10}\right)\vartheta
 =\frac{441}{5000}\vartheta.
 \tag{47}
\]
Every cell is affine in \(\vartheta\), because only one Bernoulli factor appearing to the first power varies; the nonzero coefficient in (47) proves injectivity.  Hence the image of \((-1/100,1/100)\) is a nondegenerate one-dimensional affine segment contained in the one-collision model.  When \(\vartheta\) is rational, every primitive and every full-path probability is rational, and rational \(\vartheta\)'s are dense in this interval.  This proves the stated positive-dimensional rational persistence family.  The argument establishes no relative-openness property in any larger collision variety, in agreement with the scope of the proposition.
